items.title: Luther Henderson — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: there was a guy by the name of Dick Perry... Jule used him... so if I would write for him... he would understand that expression had to be from a jazz standpoint.

ctx.x: Okay. That's great. I want to also talk about the musicians you worked with. You're coming from a era you're working with musicians who are used to that spontaneous composition, what kind of difficulties did you have in teaching non-jazz musicians that spontaneity and trying to get them to be spontaneous?

Great difficulty. Great difficulty except that in the instances where I would take the jazz musicians or jazz substance, so forth, try to use it, let's say, in the theater or in a symphonic version, that I would try most of the time to hire people, 1 or 2 at least, whose expression would come from that natural source. In other words, there was a guy by the name of Dick Perry. He happened not to be black, he was a white fellow. Very, fantastic trumpet. And Jule used him, Jule Stine used him in all of his shows…
Hold on one second, I hear a beep.
